lecons.titre: Greetings & Courtesies, Upright Joint Script, Auxiliary Verbs, and Numbers 501-600
savoirs_faire: Greet people and respond to polite greetings appropriately at different times of the day ('Good morning', 'Good afternoon', 'Good night')
Copy short texts legibly in upright joint script and write numbers in figures/words from 501 to 600
Identify and use auxiliary verbs (be, have, do) in simple sentences and read comprehension text on family

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla greets his parents in Douala: 'Good morning, Father.' Auxiliary verb: 'I AM helping mother.' Number: 550 = Five hundred and fifty.
exercices.astuce: Auxiliary verbs (am, is, are, have, do) help main verbs form tenses.

quiz.question: Which polite greeting is used when arriving at a friend's house in Douala at 8:00 AM?
quiz.explication: 'Good morning' is used before 12 noon.

quiz.question: What is the correct word form for the number 550 in English?
quiz.explication: 550 is Five hundred and fifty.

quiz.question: Which auxiliary verb correctly completes: 'She ___ doing her English homework'?
quiz.explication: 'is' forms the present continuous.

lecons.contenu:
Greetings & Courtesies, Upright Joint Script, Auxiliary Verbs, and Numbers 501-600

What you will learn:

  • Greet people and respond to polite greetings appropriately at different times of the day ('Good morning', 'Good afternoon', 'Good night')
  • Copy short texts legibly in upright joint script and write numbers in figures/words from 501 to 600
  • Identify and use auxiliary verbs (be, have, do) in simple sentences and read comprehension text on family

In Douala (Week 1, Page 4), Ekwalla greets his family appropriately, copies texts in upright joint script, uses auxiliary verbs (be, have, do), and writes numbers 501-600 in words!

lecons.titre: Songs, Multisyllabic Words, Apostrophe S', Kinds of Nouns, and Plural Formation (-es/-ies)
savoirs_faire: Sing songs using correct tones and melody, and read short texts audibly
Write sentences with apostrophe s' correctly (e.g. Ekwalla's book) and spell words with apostrophe s' through dictation
Identify and use common, proper and concrete nouns in sentences, and form plurals with -es and -ies

exercices.enonce: Fru sings a song about home in Bamenda, then writes: 'Fru's mother cooks jollof rice.' (concrete noun: rice)
exercices.astuce: Apostrophe s' shows that something belongs to someone, like Fru's mother.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses apostrophe s'?
quiz.explication: Apostrophe s' shows possession: Fru's mother.

quiz.question: Which is a concrete noun?
quiz.explication: A concrete noun names something you can touch, like rice.

quiz.question: What is the plural of 'story'?
quiz.explication: Nouns ending in a consonant + y form their plural with -ies.

lecons.contenu:
Songs, Multisyllabic Words, Apostrophe S', Kinds of Nouns, and Plural Formation (-es/-ies)

What you will learn:

  • Sing songs and read short texts audibly
  • Write sentences with apostrophe s' correctly
  • Identify common/proper/concrete nouns and form plurals with -es/-ies

In Bamenda (Week 2, Page 5), Fru sings a song about home, learns to use apostrophe s', identifies nouns, and forms plurals with -es and -ies!

lecons.titre: Traditional Songs, Apostrophe S' Practice, Kinds of Nouns, Stories, and Diphthongs 'oy'/'oi'
savoirs_faire: Sing traditional songs using correct tones and melody, and show love for reading short stories
Write sentences with apostrophe s' correctly and identify common, proper and concrete nouns in simple sentences
Read words with the diphthongs 'oy' and 'oi' (boy, coin) and use regular and irregular verbs in different sentences

exercices.enonce: Fru reads a story about a boy who finds a coin in Bamenda, then uses irregular verbs: 'He found the coin and kept it safely.'
exercices.astuce: The diphthong 'oy'/'oi' makes the same sound, as in 'boy' and 'coin'.

quiz.question: Which word contains the diphthong 'oi'?
quiz.explication: 'Coin' contains the diphthong 'oi'.

quiz.question: Which verb is irregular?
quiz.explication: 'Found' is the irregular past tense of 'find'.

quiz.question: 'Fru's story' shows what kind of noun use?
quiz.explication: Apostrophe s' shows possession.

lecons.contenu:
Traditional Songs, Apostrophe S' Practice, Kinds of Nouns, Stories, and Diphthongs 'oy'/'oi'

What you will learn:

  • Sing traditional songs and read short stories
  • Write sentences with apostrophe s' and identify nouns
  • Read the diphthongs 'oy'/'oi' and use regular/irregular verbs

In Bamenda (Week 3, Page 5), Fru sings a traditional song, reads a story about a boy and a coin, and practices apostrophe s' and irregular verbs!

lecons.titre: National Anthem, Family Dialogues, Kinds of Adjectives, and Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Sing the National Anthem of Cameroon patriotically and carry out family dialogues
Identify and use common adjectives (happy, big, clean) and proper adjectives (Cameroonian, Douala)
Write dictated sentences and complete September English integration activities

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla sings National Anthem in Douala: 'Land of promise, land of glory!' Proper adjective: Cameroonian. Common adjective: Beautiful.
exercices.astuce: Proper adjectives are derived from proper names and start with capital letters (Cameroonian).

quiz.question: Which proper adjective is derived from the proper noun 'Cameroon'?
quiz.explication: 'Cameroonian' is derived from Cameroon.

quiz.question: Why should pupils stand at attention when singing the National Anthem in Douala?
options: To show respect and patriotism for the Fatherland
quiz.explication: Standing at attention shows respect and patriotism.

quiz.question: Which word is a common descriptive adjective?
quiz.explication: 'beautiful' is a common adjective.

lecons.contenu:
National Anthem, Family Dialogues, Kinds of Adjectives, and Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Sing the National Anthem of Cameroon patriotically and carry out family dialogues
  • Identify and use common adjectives (happy, big, clean) and proper adjectives (Cameroonian, Douala)
  • Write dictated sentences and complete September English integration activities

In Douala (Week 4, Page 6), Ekwalla sings the National Anthem patriotically, uses common and proper adjectives, and completes September English with excellence!

lecons.titre: Numbers up to 5000, The 4 Math Operations, Positive Number Line (0-40), and Data Tables
savoirs_faire: Read and count numbers from 0 to 5,000 and solve problems based on the 4 operations (+, -, ×, ÷)
Add positive numbers from 0 to 40 on the Number Line
Introduction to graphs and statistics by collecting data and representing on a table

exercices.enonce: Ndombe counts numbers in Douala: Read 4,500. Number line: 15 + 20 = 35. 4 rules: 2500 + 1500 = 4000.
exercices.astuce: The number line represents numbers in sequential order from left to right.

quiz.question: What is the standard numerical form of Four thousand five hundred?
quiz.explication: Four thousand five hundred is 4500.

quiz.question: What is 15 + 20 added on a positive number line?
What are the four basic operations of Mathematics?
quiz.explication: +, -, ×, ÷ are the 4 basic math operations.

lecons.contenu:
Numbers up to 5000, The 4 Math Operations, Positive Number Line (0-40), and Data Tables

What you will learn:

  • Read and count numbers from 0 to 5,000 and solve problems based on the 4 operations (+, -, ×, ÷)
  • Add positive numbers from 0 to 40 on the Number Line
  • Introduction to graphs and statistics by collecting data and representing on a table

In Douala (Week 1, Page 20), Ndombe reads numbers up to 5,000, solves 4-operation problems, adds positive numbers on the number line (0-40), and collects data into tables!

lecons.titre: Math & Set Symbols, Length Unit Conversions (m, cm, mm), and Negative Number Subtraction
savoirs_faire: Identify mathematical symbols (=, ≠, <, >) and set symbols (∈, ∉, ∅)
Convert length metric units (meters to centimeters: 1 m = 100 cm, cm to mm: 1 cm = 10 mm)
Subtract negative numbers on the number line 0 - (-40) and state difference between graphs and statistics

exercices.enonce: Ndombe converts length in Douala: 3 meters = 300 cm. Set symbol: ∈ means 'is an element of'.
exercices.astuce: 1 meter (m) = 100 centimeters (cm).

quiz.question: How many centimeters (cm) are equal to 3 meters (m)?
Which set symbol means 'is an element of'?
quiz.explication: ∈ represents element membership.

quiz.question: Which mathematical symbol represents 'is not equal to'?
quiz.explication: ≠ means not equal to.

lecons.contenu:
Math & Set Symbols, Length Unit Conversions (m, cm, mm), and Negative Number Subtraction

What you will learn:

  • Identify mathematical symbols (=, ≠, <, >) and set symbols (∈, ∉, ∅)
  • Convert length metric units (meters to centimeters: 1 m = 100 cm, cm to mm: 1 cm = 10 mm)
  • Subtract negative numbers on the number line 0 - (-40) and state difference between graphs and statistics

In Douala (Week 2, Page 20), Ndombe identifies math and set symbols, converts meters to centimeters, subtracts negative numbers, and differentiates graphs from statistics!

lecons.titre: Expanded Form of 4-Digit Numbers, Meters to Centimeters, Number Line Points, and Coordinate Axes
savoirs_faire: Write 4-digit numbers in expanded form (e.g. 4325 = 4000 + 300 + 20 + 5) and standard form
Convert meters to centimeters and locate marked points on the number line up to 20
Use coordinates (x, y) to locate axes and the origin (0,0), and represent data sets on a table

exercices.enonce: Ndombe expands numbers in Douala: 4325 = 4000 + 300 + 20 + 5. Origin coordinates = (0,0).
exercices.astuce: Expanded form breaks down a number into the value of each digit.

quiz.question: What is the expanded form of the 4-digit number 4325?
What are the coordinate values of the Origin point on an x,y coordinate plane?
quiz.explication: (0,0) is the Origin.

quiz.question: How many centimeters are in 5 meters?

lecons.contenu:
Expanded Form of 4-Digit Numbers, Meters to Centimeters, Number Line Points, and Coordinate Axes

What you will learn:

  • Write 4-digit numbers in expanded form (e.g. 4325 = 4000 + 300 + 20 + 5) and standard form
  • Convert meters to centimeters and locate marked points on the number line up to 20
  • Use coordinates (x, y) to locate axes and the origin (0,0), and represent data sets on a table

In Douala (Week 3, Page 20-21), Ndombe writes 4-digit numbers in expanded form (4325 = 4000+300+20+5), converts meters to cm, locates points on number lines, and uses coordinate axes!

lecons.titre: 4-Digit Subtraction with Borrowing, Meters to Kilometers, and Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Construct and use subtraction tables and perform 4-digit subtraction with borrowing under Th H T U
Convert meters to kilometers (1000 m = 1 km e.g. 3000 m = 3 km)
Use coordinates to locate marked points and complete September math integration activities and assessment

exercices.enonce: Ndombe converts distance in Douala: 3000 meters = 3 kilometers. Subtraction: 5432 - 2819 = 2613.
exercices.astuce: 1 kilometer (km) = 1000 meters (m).

quiz.question: How many kilometers (km) are equal to 3000 meters (m)?
What is 5432 - 2819 in 4-digit subtraction?
How many meters are in 4.5 kilometers?

lecons.contenu:
4-Digit Subtraction with Borrowing, Meters to Kilometers, and Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Construct and use subtraction tables and perform 4-digit subtraction with borrowing under Th H T U
  • Convert meters to kilometers (1000 m = 1 km e.g. 3000 m = 3 km)
  • Use coordinates to locate marked points and complete September math integration activities and assessment

In Douala (Week 4, Page 21), Ndombe performs 4-digit subtraction with borrowing, converts meters to kilometers (3000 m = 3 km), uses coordinates, and completes September math with excellence!

lecons.titre: Parts of the Body, Sources of Energy, and the Immediate Environment
savoirs_faire: List the main parts of the human body (head, trunk, arms, legs, sense organs)
Describe sources of energy (the sun, food, fire from wood, kerosene, electricity)
Know and describe the immediate environment (home, compound, neighbourhood)

exercices.enonce: Ateba in Douala lists his body parts (head, arms, legs), then lights a kerosene lamp: 'The lamp gives us light and heat energy.'
exercices.astuce: Energy can come from the sun, food, fire, or electricity — it helps us do work.

quiz.question: Which of these is a part of the body?
quiz.explication: The head is a main part of the human body.

quiz.question: Which of these is a source of energy?
quiz.explication: The sun gives light and heat energy.

quiz.question: What is your immediate environment?
quiz.explication: The immediate environment is the place close to where you live.

lecons.contenu:
Parts of the Body, Sources of Energy, and the Immediate Environment

What you will learn:

  • List the main parts of the body
  • Describe sources of energy
  • Describe your immediate environment

In Douala (Week 1, Page 29), Ateba names his body parts, lights a kerosene lamp to learn about energy, and describes his home environment!

lecons.titre: Functions of Body Parts, the Importance of Energy, and Domestic vs Wild Animals
savoirs_faire: State how the various parts of the body function (legs for walking, hands for holding, eyes for seeing)
State the importance of energy (cooking food, lighting homes, running machines)
Differentiate between domestic animals (cow, goat, dog) and wild animals (lion, elephant, monkey)

exercices.enonce: Ateba's legs help him walk to school in Douala. His mother uses fire energy to cook. He sees a dog (domestic) and a monkey (wild) near the forest.
exercices.astuce: Domestic animals live with and are cared for by people; wild animals live freely in nature.

quiz.question: What do we use our legs for?
quiz.explication: Legs are used for walking and moving.

quiz.question: Why is energy important?
options: It helps cook food and light homes
quiz.explication: Energy is used for cooking, lighting, and running machines.

quiz.question: Which of these is a domestic animal?
quiz.explication: A cow is a domestic animal cared for by people.

lecons.contenu:
Functions of Body Parts, the Importance of Energy, and Domestic vs Wild Animals

What you will learn:

  • Learn the functions of body parts
  • State the importance of energy
  • Differentiate domestic and wild animals

In Douala (Week 2, Page 29), Ateba learns how his body parts function, why energy matters, and the difference between domestic and wild animals!

lecons.titre: Care of Body Parts, Forms of Energy, and Drugs and Drug Abuse
savoirs_faire: Enumerate ways of cleaning and caring for the body (washing, brushing teeth, trimming nails)
State the various forms of energy (heat, light, electrical, mechanical)
Know what drugs are and understand what amounts to drug abuse

exercices.enonce: Ateba washes his body and brushes his teeth every morning in Douala. His teacher explains that using medicine without a doctor's advice is drug abuse.
exercices.astuce: Drugs used the wrong way, or without a doctor's advice, can harm the body — that is drug abuse.

quiz.question: Which of these keeps the body clean?
quiz.explication: Washing and brushing teeth keep the body clean and healthy.

quiz.question: Which of these is a form of energy?
quiz.explication: Heat is a form of energy.

quiz.question: What is drug abuse?
options: Using drugs the wrong way or without a doctor's advice
Taking medicine prescribed by a doctor
quiz.explication: Drug abuse means misusing drugs in a way that harms the body.

lecons.contenu:
Care of Body Parts, Forms of Energy, and Drugs and Drug Abuse

What you will learn:

  • Learn how to care for your body
  • Discover forms of energy
  • Understand what drug abuse means

In Douala (Week 3, Page 29), Ateba learns to care for his body, discovers different forms of energy, and learns what drug abuse means!

lecons.titre: Advantages of Energy and the Effects of Drugs: Integration and Remediation
savoirs_faire: State the advantages of energy in daily life (cooking, lighting, transportation, communication)
Enumerate the negative effects of drugs on the body and on daily life
Apply knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired this month to daily life situations (integration, assessment and remediation)

exercices.enonce: Ateba explains in Douala how energy helps his family cook and light their home, then lists why drug abuse is dangerous for health.
exercices.astuce: Energy makes daily life easier, but misused drugs can seriously harm the body.

quiz.question: Which is an advantage of energy?
options: It helps cook food and light homes
quiz.explication: Energy helps with cooking, lighting, and many daily tasks.

quiz.question: What can be a negative effect of drug abuse?
options: Harm to the body and health
quiz.explication: Drug abuse can seriously harm the body and health.

quiz.question: What should you do during an integration and remediation week?
options: Apply what you learned to daily life
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the month's lessons to real daily life situations.

lecons.contenu:
Advantages of Energy and the Effects of Drugs: Integration and Remediation

What you will learn:

  • State the advantages of energy
  • Learn the negative effects of drugs
  • Review the month's lessons about The Home

In Douala (Week 4, Page 30), Ateba reviews the advantages of energy and the dangers of drug abuse, closing the month on The Home!

lecons.titre: La maison et la famille, salutations/présentations, lexique de la famille, et les articles définis
savoirs_faire: Saluer, se présenter et présenter les membres de sa famille et leur profession ('Bonjour, voici mon père et ma mère')
Enrichir son vocabulaire familial (père, mère, oncle, tante, cousin, nièce, profession)
Utiliser correctement les articles définis (le, la, l', les) et identifier le groupe nominal dans une phrase

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla présente sa famille à Douala (Cameroun), dans le salon : 'Bonjour, voici MON père (professeur) et MA mère (infirmière), MON oncle et MA tante.'
exercices.astuce: Articles définis : LE (masculin), LA (féminin), L' (devant voyelle), LES (pluriel).

quiz.question: Quel article défini convient devant le nom féminin 'tante' ?
quiz.explication: 'tante' est un nom féminin (la tante).

quiz.question: Comment salue-t-on quelqu'un le matin en français ?
quiz.explication: 'Bonjour' est la salutation du matin/de la journée.

quiz.question: Quel mot désigne le frère du père ou de la mère ?
quiz.explication: L'oncle est le frère du père ou de la mère.

lecons.contenu:
La maison et la famille, salutations/présentations, lexique de la famille, et les articles définis

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Saluer, se présenter et présenter les membres de sa famille
  • Enrichir son vocabulaire familial (père, mère, oncle, tante, cousin, nièce)
  • Utiliser correctement les articles définis (le, la, l', les)

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaine 1, Page 37), Ekwalla présente sa famille dans le salon, apprend le lexique familial, et utilise les articles définis (le, la, les) !

lecons.titre: La cuisine et les toilettes, salutations avancées, se présenter, adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs
savoirs_faire: Utiliser des salutations avancées (bonne après-midi, bonne nuit, comment allez-vous, comment ça va) et reconnaître les types de noms
Se présenter et présenter ses camarades ('je m'appelle', 'il/elle s'appelle', 'j'habite à')
Employer les adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs, et utiliser correctement les antonymes

exercices.enonce: Dans la cuisine puis dans les toilettes de sa maison à Douala, Ekwalla dit : 'Bonne après-midi ! Je m'appelle Ekwalla, j'habite à Douala. CETTE cuisine est propre (antonyme de sale).'
exercices.astuce: Adjectifs possessifs : mon/ma/mes, son/sa/ses. Adjectifs démonstratifs : ce, cette, ces.

quiz.question: Comment dit-on 'Comment allez-vous' de façon informelle ?
quiz.explication: 'Comment ça va' est la forme informelle de 'Comment allez-vous'.

quiz.question: Comment dit-on son propre nom en français ?
quiz.explication: 'Je m'appelle...' sert à donner son propre nom.

quiz.question: Quel est l'antonyme (contraire) de 'propre' ?
quiz.explication: 'Sale' est le contraire de 'propre'.

lecons.contenu:
La cuisine et les toilettes, salutations avancées, se présenter, adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser des salutations avancées et reconnaître les types de noms
  • Se présenter avec 'je m'appelle' et 'j'habite à'
  • Employer les adjectifs possessifs, démonstratifs et les antonymes

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaines 2-3, Pages 39-41), Ekwalla utilise des salutations avancées dans la cuisine, se présente dans les toilettes, et emploie adjectifs possessifs, démonstratifs et antonymes !

lecons.titre: Les objets de la concession, le vocabulaire de la météo, et évaluation de septembre
savoirs_faire: Parler du temps qu'il fait (il pleut, il fait beau, il neige, il fait froid, il fait chaud)
Lire des textes divers relatifs aux objets de la concession et regrouper des mots par famille
Réaliser l'évaluation et la remédiation de septembre

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla observe les objets de la concession familiale à Douala et parle du temps : 'Aujourd'hui, IL FAIT BEAU. Hier, IL PLEUVAIT.'
exercices.astuce: Vocabulaire météo : il pleut, il fait beau, il neige, il fait froid, il fait chaud.

quiz.question: Comment dit-on qu'il y a de la pluie ?
quiz.explication: 'Il pleut' indique la présence de pluie.

quiz.question: Quelle expression décrit un temps ensoleillé et agréable ?
quiz.explication: 'Il fait beau' décrit un temps ensoleillé et agréable.

quiz.question: À quoi sert l'évaluation de fin de mois ?
options: À vérifier ce qui a été appris et à corriger les lacunes
À apprendre un tout nouveau sujet
quiz.explication: L'évaluation et la remédiation permettent de vérifier les acquis et de corriger les lacunes.

lecons.contenu:
Les objets de la concession, le vocabulaire de la météo, et évaluation de septembre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Parler du temps qu'il fait
  • Lire des textes sur les objets de la concession
  • Réaliser l'évaluation et la remédiation de septembre

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaine 4, Page 42), Ekwalla observe les objets de la concession, parle du temps qu'il fait, et réalise l'évaluation de septembre !

lecons.titre: The Definition and Types of History, Reasons for Studying Geography, the Flag of Cameroon, and Greetings
savoirs_faire: Define history and name its types (political, social, economic history)
Define geography and state reasons for studying it
Define the colours of the Cameroon flag and the correct standing position when it is hoisted, and say how to greet

exercices.enonce: Tanyi's teacher in Foumban defines history as the study of past events, and geography as the study of the Earth and its people. Tanyi then names the colours of the flag (green, red, yellow) and stands correctly during the flag hoisting, and greets a visitor politely.
exercices.astuce: History studies past events; geography studies the Earth, its features, and its people.

quiz.question: What is history?
quiz.explication: History is the study of past events and how they shaped the present.

quiz.question: Why do we study geography?
options: To understand the Earth, its features and its people
quiz.explication: Geography helps us understand the Earth's features, climate, and people.

quiz.question: What are the colours of the Cameroon flag?
quiz.explication: The Cameroon flag has three colours: green, red, and yellow, with a yellow star.

lecons.contenu:
The Definition and Types of History, Reasons for Studying Geography, the Flag of Cameroon, and Greetings

What you will learn:

  • Define history and name its types
  • State reasons for studying geography
  • Name the colours of the flag and the correct standing position, and say how to greet

In Foumban (Week 1, Page 86), Tanyi learns what history and geography are, names the colours of the Cameroon flag, and greets politely!

lecons.titre: The Notion of Time in History, the Meaning of Weather, the Flag of Cameroon, and Greetings
savoirs_faire: Explain dates and periods in history (the notion of time)
Define weather and give reasons for studying it
Name the colours of the flag and the correct standing position when it is hoisted, and say how to greet

exercices.enonce: Tanyi's teacher in Foumban explains that history uses dates and periods to order past events. Tanyi then learns that weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere, and reviews the flag colours and how to greet an elder respectfully.
exercices.astuce: History uses dates and periods (the notion of time) to place events in the correct order.

quiz.question: Why do historians use dates and periods?
options: To place past events in the correct order
quiz.explication: Dates and periods (the notion of time) help order historical events correctly.

quiz.question: What is weather?
options: The day-to-day state of the atmosphere
quiz.explication: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere (sun, rain, wind).

quiz.question: How should pupils stand when the flag is hoisted?
quiz.explication: Pupils stand still and attentively as a sign of respect when the flag is hoisted.

lecons.contenu:
The Notion of Time in History, the Meaning of Weather, the Flag of Cameroon, and Greetings

What you will learn:

  • Explain dates and periods in history
  • Define weather and reasons for studying it
  • Review the flag and how to greet respectfully

In Foumban (Week 2, Page 86), Tanyi learns about dates and periods in history, discovers what weather means, and reviews the flag and greetings!

lecons.titre: The Early Man and His Characteristics, Weather Elements, Administrative Rulers, and Children's Rights
savoirs_faire: Say who the early man was and describe his characteristics
List and explain the elements of weather (sun, rain, wind, temperature)
Name and identify administrative rulers, and state the rights of a child

exercices.enonce: Tanyi's teacher in Foumban describes the early man as the first human beings who lived long ago and looked different from people today. Tanyi then names the elements of weather (sun, rain, wind), learns about administrative rulers like the Divisional Officer, and lists the rights of a child (education, health, protection).
exercices.astuce: The early man refers to the first human beings who lived a very long time ago.

quiz.question: Who was the early man?
options: The first human beings who lived long ago
quiz.explication: The early man refers to the first human beings who lived a very long time ago.

quiz.question: Which of these is an element of weather?
quiz.explication: Rain, sun, and wind are elements of weather.

quiz.question: Which of these is a right of a child?
options: The right to skip school forever
quiz.explication: Every child has the right to education, health, and protection.

lecons.contenu:
The Early Man and His Characteristics, Weather Elements, Administrative Rulers, and Children's Rights

What you will learn:

  • Learn who the early man was and his characteristics
  • List and explain elements of weather
  • Identify administrative rulers and state the rights of a child

In Foumban (Week 3, Page 86), Tanyi learns about the early man, discovers the elements of weather, and learns the rights of a child!

lecons.titre: Early Man Discoveries, Fabricating Weather Instruments, National Anthem, and Integration
savoirs_faire: List all major tools and discoveries of Early Man (stone axes, fire, clay pottery, bow and arrows)
Fabricate simple weather instruments (homemade rain gauge using plastic bottles)
Sing the National Anthem correctly, practice apologies etiquette, and complete September social studies integration

exercices.enonce: Tanyi fabricates a rain gauge in Foumban: Cut top of plastic bottle, invert funnel inside, mark millimeter scale.
exercices.astuce: A homemade rain gauge uses a plastic bottle with an inverted funnel top.

quiz.question: What simple recycled item can be used by pupils to fabricate a homemade rain gauge?
options: A clear plastic bottle with an inverted funnel top
quiz.explication: Plastic bottles make excellent homemade rain gauges.

quiz.question: What is the polite ethical word spoken when making an apology for a mistake?
quiz.explication: 'I am sorry' expresses sincere apology.

quiz.question: Which early discovery allowed Early Man to store water and cook food over fire?
quiz.explication: Clay pottery allowed storing water and cooking.

lecons.contenu:
Early Man Discoveries, Fabricating Weather Instruments, National Anthem, and Integration

lecons.titre: Input vs. Output Devices & Their Importance

quiz.question: Which of these computer hardware components is an INPUT device used for entering text data in Douala?

quiz.question: Which hardware component is an OUTPUT device used for printing documents onto paper?

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a computer Monitor?

Input vs. Output Devices & Their Importance

lecons.titre: Operating Systems (Windows & Linux/Ubuntu)

Identify popular operating systems (Microsoft Windows, Linux/Ubuntu, macOS, Android)

quiz.explication: Operating Systems manage all hardware/software.

quiz.question: Which of the following is an open-source Linux Operating System commonly used in schools?
quiz.explication: Ubuntu is a popular Linux OS.

quiz.question: What happens when a computer has no Operating System installed?

Operating Systems (Windows & Linux/Ubuntu)

In Douala (Week 2, Page 128), Kotto defines Operating Systems (Windows, Ubuntu), describes OS functions, and identifies master system software!

quiz.question: Which inbuilt computer component is known as the 'Brain of the Computer' that processes all calculations?
quiz.explication: CPU is the processing brain of the computer.

quiz.question: Which component stores documents, photos, and programs permanently on a computer?
quiz.explication: Hard Drives provide permanent storage.

quiz.question: What is the function of RAM (Random Access Memory) in a computer?
options: Holding active data temporarily while applications are running
quiz.explication: RAM holds active application data temporarily.

Inbuilt Computer Components (CPU, RAM, Hard Drive)

  • Define and describe characteristics of computer inbuilt components: CPU (Central Processing Unit / Brain), RAM (Random Access Memory), Hard Drive (Storage)

quiz.question: Which computer type is recommended for a teacher who needs to carry a computer between classrooms in Douala?

quiz.question: Why is having sufficient RAM capacity (e.g. 8 GB RAM) important when buying a computer?
options: It allows the computer to run multiple applications smoothly without slowing down

lecons.titre: Polite Language, Things Found in Town, the Pattern 'th', and the Simple Present Tense
savoirs_faire: Use polite forms of request and response, and address people appropriately
Describe life in Town and read sentences with the pattern 'th'
Write sentences and paragraphs about a Town using the simple present tense

exercices.astuce: The pattern 'th' can sound soft (three) or hard (this) — listen carefully.

quiz.question: Which is a polite request?

quiz.question: Which word has the pattern 'th'?
quiz.explication: 'Three' contains the pattern 'th'.

quiz.question: 'The market opens every day' uses which tense?
quiz.explication: The simple present tense describes regular actions.

Polite Language, Things Found in Town, the Pattern 'th', and the Simple Present Tense

savoirs_faire: Carry out a dialogue about personalities in Town, and read short texts with the 'ch' sound
Write numbers in figures and words from 100 to 200
Manipulate verbs in the simple past tense and deduce a moral lesson from a cartoon

exercices.astuce: The simple past tense describes actions that already finished, like 'visited'.

quiz.question: Which word has the 'ch' sound?
quiz.explication: 'Chief' contains the 'ch' sound.

quiz.question: How do you write '150' in words?
quiz.explication: 150 is written 'one hundred and fifty'.

quiz.question: 'The Mayor visited the school' uses which tense?
quiz.explication: 'Visited' is the simple past tense.

Personalities in Town, the Sound 'ch', Numbers 100-200, and the Simple Past Tense

lecons.titre: Things Found in the Village, Phonics Sound 'sh', Comparative & Superlative Adjectives, and Adventure Stories
savoirs_faire: Describe life and things found in the village (farms, thatched huts, streams, traditional shrines, palm trees)
Identify and pronounce words with the sound 'sh' (shoe, shop, fish, dish, shell)
Construct sentences using comparative adjectives (-er / more e.g. taller, more beautiful) and superlative adjectives (-est / most e.g. tallest, most peaceful)

exercices.astuce: Comparative (-er/more) compares 2 items; Superlative (-est/most) compares 3 or more.

quiz.question: Which comparative adjective correctly completes: 'The village air is ___ than town air'?
quiz.explication: 'cleaner' compares two items.

quiz.question: Which word features the 'sh' sound pattern?
quiz.explication: 'Shop' and 'Fish' contain the 'sh' sound.

quiz.question: Which superlative adjective completes: 'Mount Cameroon is the ___ mountain in West Africa'?

Things Found in the Village, Phonics Sound 'sh', Comparative & Superlative Adjectives, and Adventure Stories

lecons.titre: Phonics Sound /ai/, Narrative Essays (80 words), Plural Formation, Village Debate, and Integration
savoirs_faire: Identify and pronounce words with the sound /ai/ (cry, sky, fly, dry, high)

quiz.question: What is the correct plural form of the noun 'city'?
quiz.explication: 'city' becomes 'cities'.

quiz.question: Which word features the vowel sound /ai/?

quiz.question: What is the plural of 'bush'?
quiz.explication: Nouns ending in -sh add -es (bushes).

lecons.contenu:
Phonics Sound /ai/, Narrative Essays (80 words), Plural Formation, Village Debate, and Integration

lecons.titre: Multiplication of 4-Digit Numbers, Set Types, Length Addition, and Frequency Tables

Name different types of sets (finite set, infinite set, empty set)
Add lengths using metric units (meters and centimeters) and add numbers using the number line and frequency tables

What is 4 m 50 cm + 3 m 25 cm in length addition?
Which set type has elements that can be counted to a final number?

Multiplication of 4-Digit Numbers, Set Types, Length Addition, and Frequency Tables

lecons.titre: Division of Numbers, Set Formation, Length Subtraction, and Finding Averages (Mean)
savoirs_faire: Divide numbers and solve capacity division problems
Demonstrate formation of sets from given groups of objects
Subtract lengths (e.g. 10 m 80 cm - 4 m 30 cm = 6 m 50 cm), subtract using number lines, and calculate Averages (Mean)

  • Demonstrate formation of sets from given groups of objects
  • Subtract lengths (e.g. 10 m 80 cm - 4 m 30 cm = 6 m 50 cm), subtract using number lines, and calculate Averages (Mean)

In Douala (Week 3, Page 21-22), Ndombe compares numbers with < and >, states set elements, multiplies lengths, identifies parallel vs. intersecting lines, and solves advanced average problems!

lecons.titre: Place Value Chart to 10,000, Length Division, Counting Unit Squares for Area, and Integration

Place Value Chart to 10,000, Length Division, Counting Unit Squares for Area, and Integration

quiz.question: Which of these can cause a health hazard?

The Five Senses (Functions and Care), Machines and their Types, and Health Hazards

State the causes and effects of land pollution (dumping rubbish, plastic waste)

Bones and their Types, Parts of a Machine, and Land Pollution
