exercices.astuce: Learning about body parts, including reproductive organs, is part of understanding how the human body works.

quiz.question: Learning about the reproductive organs is part of what subject?
quiz.explication: The reproductive system is studied as part of health education and science.

quiz.question: What material is commonly used for weaving a basket?
quiz.explication: Baskets are traditionally woven from bamboo or fibre.

quiz.question: Why is gardening important?
quiz.explication: Gardening provides food (vegetables) and beauty (flowers).

lecons.contenu:
The Male Reproductive Organs, Weaving a Basket, and Types and Importance of Gardening

What you will learn:

  • Learn about the male reproductive organs at a basic level
  • Practice weaving a basket
  • Discover types of gardening and their importance

In Bamenda (Week 2, Page 31), Fon learns about the human body's reproductive system, weaves a basket, and helps in the school garden!

lecons.titre: The Female Reproductive Organs, Weaving a Basket, and Types of Plants
savoirs_faire: Identify the female reproductive organs at a basic, age-appropriate level (part of the human reproductive system)
Complete the production of a woven basket using local materials
Identify the different types of plants (trees, shrubs, herbs, climbers)

exercices.enonce: Fon's teacher in Bamenda continues the body science lesson with a labelled diagram, explaining that both male and female bodies have reproductive organs that allow humans to reproduce. Fon finishes weaving his basket and identifies a tree, a shrub, and a climbing plant near the school.
exercices.astuce: Both male and female bodies have reproductive organs — this is a normal part of how the human body works.

quiz.question: Both male and female bodies have reproductive organs. What is their role?
quiz.explication: Reproductive organs allow living things, including humans, to reproduce.

quiz.question: Which of these is a type of plant?
quiz.explication: A tree is a type of plant.

quiz.question: Which plant type climbs on supports?
quiz.explication: Climbers are plants that grow by climbing on supports.

lecons.contenu:
The Female Reproductive Organs, Weaving a Basket, and Types of Plants

What you will learn:

  • Learn about the female reproductive organs at a basic level
  • Complete a woven basket
  • Identify types of plants

In Bamenda (Week 3, Page 31), Fon continues learning about the human body, finishes weaving his basket, and identifies different types of plants!

lecons.titre: Caring for the Reproductive Organs, Weaving a Raffia Bag: Integration and Remediation
savoirs_faire: Say how to care for the reproductive organs (personal cleanliness, hygiene) and explain this to others
Produce a raffia bag using weaving techniques learned this month
Apply knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired this month to daily life situations (integration, assessment and remediation)

exercices.enonce: Fon's teacher in Bamenda explains that keeping the whole body clean, including washing daily, is important for the reproductive organs too. Fon completes a raffia bag using the weaving skills learned this month.
exercices.astuce: Daily washing and general body hygiene are the main ways to care for the reproductive organs, just like any other body part.

quiz.question: How should the reproductive organs be cared for?
options: Through daily washing and good hygiene
quiz.explication: Good personal hygiene, including daily washing, cares for all body parts including the reproductive organs.

quiz.question: What is Fon making by the end of the month?
quiz.explication: Fon weaves a raffia bag using local materials.

quiz.question: What should you do during an integration and remediation week?
options: Apply what you learned to daily life
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the month's lessons to real daily life situations.

lecons.contenu:
Caring for the Reproductive Organs, Weaving a Raffia Bag: Integration and Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Learn how to care for the reproductive organs through hygiene
  • Complete a raffia bag
  • Review the month's lessons about School

In Bamenda (Week 4, Page 31), Fon learns about body hygiene, finishes his raffia bag, and reviews everything learned this month about School!

lecons.titre: Les membres de la famille de l'école, décrire une personne, et les marques régulières du pluriel
savoirs_faire: Décrire un objet, un paysage ou une personne (aspect général, physique, moral)
Organiser un récit dans un ordre chronologique cohérent en utilisant le dictionnaire bilingue
Utiliser correctement les signes de ponctuation (interrogation, exclamation) et les marques régulières du pluriel (-x, -aux)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla décrit les membres de la famille de son école à Douala : 'Mon maître est GRAND et GENTIL (aspect physique et moral). Les CHEVAUX du dessin sont beaux (pluriel en -aux).'
exercices.astuce: Les noms en -al forment souvent leur pluriel en -aux (cheval → chevaux).

quiz.question: Quel mot décrit l'aspect moral d'une personne ?
quiz.explication: 'Gentil' décrit le caractère (aspect moral), tandis que 'grand' décrit l'aspect physique.

quiz.question: Quel est le pluriel de 'cheval' ?
quiz.explication: Les noms en -al forment leur pluriel en -aux (cheval → chevaux).

quiz.question: Quel outil aide à trouver le sens d'un mot inconnu ?
quiz.explication: Le dictionnaire bilingue aide à comprendre et traduire les mots.

lecons.contenu:
Les membres de la famille de l'école, décrire une personne, et les marques régulières du pluriel

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Décrire une personne (aspect général, physique, moral)
  • Organiser un récit en utilisant le dictionnaire bilingue
  • Utiliser les signes de ponctuation et les marques régulières du pluriel

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaine 1, Page 49), Ekwalla décrit les membres de la famille de son école, utilise le dictionnaire bilingue, et apprend les marques du pluriel !

lecons.titre: La structure de l'école, décrire avec 'il est/il a', les couleurs, et le son [ienetein]
savoirs_faire: Décrire avec les structures 'il est...', 'il a...', 'elle/il est sympa/triste'
Nommer des animaux et des couleurs, et raconter un fait divers dans l'ordre chronologique
Identifier et prononcer les mots avec le son [ienetein] (chien, chrétien, haleine, peine) et reconnaître la phrase déclarative

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla décrit la structure de son école à Douala : 'Le directeur EST sympa, IL A un grand bureau. Mon CHIEN [son ienetein] m'attend à la sortie.'
exercices.astuce: Structures de description : 'il est...' (qualité), 'il a...' (possession).

quiz.question: Quelle structure sert à exprimer une possession ?
quiz.explication: 'Il a...' exprime la possession, contrairement à 'il est...' qui exprime une qualité.

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots contient le son [ienetein] ?
quiz.explication: 'Chien' contient le son [ienetein].

quiz.question: Qu'est-ce qu'une phrase déclarative ?
options: Une phrase qui affirme quelque chose et se termine par un point
Une phrase qui pose une question
Une phrase qui exprime un ordre
quiz.explication: Une phrase déclarative affirme un fait et se termine généralement par un point.

lecons.contenu:
La structure de l'école, décrire avec 'il est/il a', les couleurs, et le son [ienetein]

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Décrire avec 'il est...' et 'il a...'
  • Nommer des animaux, des couleurs et raconter un fait divers
  • Identifier le son [ienetein] et la phrase déclarative

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaine 2, Page 51), Ekwalla découvre la structure de son école, décrit avec 'il est/il a', et identifie le son [ienetein] !

lecons.titre: Les activités et les règles de l'école, les sons [tr]/[dr] et [ai]/[ia], la phrase interrogative et exclamative, et évaluation de novembre
savoirs_faire: Organiser un récit sur les activités de l'école dans un ordre cohérent et identifier la phrase interrogative
Identifier et prononcer les mots avec les sons [tr]/[dr] (drapeau, travail) et [ai]/[ia]
Accorder correctement les adjectifs qualificatifs et démonstratifs, reconnaître la phrase exclamative, et réaliser l'évaluation de novembre

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla raconte les activités et les règles de son école à Douala : 'Le TRAVAIL commence à 8 heures ! (phrase exclamative). Est-ce que tu as vu le DRAPEAU ? (phrase interrogative)'
exercices.astuce: Les sons [tr] et [dr] : travail, drapeau. Une phrase exclamative se termine par un point d'exclamation (!).

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots contient le son [dr] ?
quiz.explication: 'Drapeau' contient le son [dr].

quiz.question: Quel signe termine une phrase interrogative ?
quiz.explication: Une phrase interrogative se termine par un point d'interrogation (?).

quiz.question: À quoi sert l'évaluation de fin de mois ?
options: À vérifier les acquis et corriger les lacunes
À apprendre un tout nouveau sujet
quiz.explication: L'évaluation et la remédiation permettent de vérifier les acquis et de corriger les lacunes.

lecons.contenu:
Les activités et les règles de l'école, les sons [tr]/[dr] et [ai]/[ia], la phrase interrogative et exclamative, et évaluation de novembre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Raconter les activités de l'école et identifier la phrase interrogative
  • Identifier les sons [tr]/[dr] et [ai]/[ia]
  • Reconnaître la phrase exclamative et réaliser l'évaluation de novembre

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaines 3-4, Pages 54-58), Ekwalla raconte les activités et les règles de son école, identifie les sons [tr]/[dr] et [ai]/[ia], et réalise l'évaluation de novembre !

lecons.titre: The Discovery and Naming of Cameroon, Location of Vegetation Types, Administrative Structure of a Region, and Human Right Abuse
savoirs_faire: Trace the process leading to the naming of Cameroon
Draw and locate the types of vegetation on the Cameroon map
Describe the administrative structure of a region and describe human right abuse

exercices.enonce: Ndombe's teacher in Douala explains that Portuguese explorers named the Wouri river 'Rio dos Camaroes' (river of prawns), which gave Cameroon its name. Ndombe then locates the forest and savannah zones on a map, and learns that hitting or shouting insults at someone is a human right abuse.
exercices.astuce: Cameroon's name comes from 'Rio dos Camaroes', Portuguese for 'river of prawns', named after the Wouri river.

quiz.question: Where does the name 'Cameroon' come from?
options: 'Rio dos Camaroes' (river of prawns) given by Portuguese explorers
quiz.explication: Portuguese explorers named the Wouri river 'Rio dos Camaroes', which became 'Cameroon'.

quiz.question: What does a map help us do with vegetation?
options: Locate where different vegetation types are found
quiz.explication: A map helps locate where forests, savannahs, and other vegetation types are found.

quiz.question: What is human right abuse?
options: Treating a person unfairly or harmfully, violating their basic rights
quiz.explication: Human right abuse means treating a person unfairly or harmfully, violating their basic rights.

lecons.contenu:
The Discovery and Naming of Cameroon, Location of Vegetation Types, Administrative Structure of a Region, and Human Right Abuse

What you will learn:

  • Trace how Cameroon got its name
  • Locate vegetation types on a map
  • Describe a region's administrative structure and human right abuse

In Douala (Week 1, Page 88), Ndombe learns how Cameroon got its name, locates vegetation on a map, and learns about human right abuse!

lecons.titre: The Arrival of the Carthaginians in Cameroon, the Forest and Its Importance, the Seal, and Care
savoirs_faire: Narrate the arrival of the Carthaginians in Cameroon
Define the forest and explain its importance
Say what the seal is and the importance of national emblems, and practice ethical values of care

exercices.enonce: Ndombe's teacher in Douala tells the story of the Carthaginians, ancient sailors who reached the Cameroon coast long ago. Ndombe then learns that forests give wood, clean the air, and shelter animals, and that the national seal is an official symbol used to authenticate government documents.
exercices.astuce: The seal is an official emblem used to authenticate important government documents.

quiz.question: Who were the Carthaginians?
options: Ancient sailors who reached the Cameroon coast long ago
quiz.explication: The Carthaginians were ancient sailors who are said to have reached the Cameroon coast long ago.

quiz.question: Why is the forest important?
options: It gives wood, cleans the air, and shelters animals
quiz.explication: The forest is important because it gives wood, cleans the air, and shelters animals.

quiz.question: What is the seal used for?
quiz.explication: The national seal is an official emblem used to authenticate government documents.

lecons.contenu:
The Arrival of the Carthaginians in Cameroon, the Forest and Its Importance, the Seal, and Care

What you will learn:

  • Learn about the arrival of the Carthaginians
  • Discover the forest and its importance
  • Learn what the seal is and practice care

In Douala (Week 2, Page 89), Ndombe learns about the Carthaginians, discovers why the forest matters, and learns about the national seal!

lecons.titre: The Exploration of Cameroon, Afforestation and Deforestation, Municipal Elections, and Sexual Abuse
savoirs_faire: Explain how Europeans explored Cameroon
Define deforestation and its effects
Define and explain the municipal electoral process, and say what sexual abuse means and its consequences

exercices.enonce: Ndombe's teacher in Douala explains that European explorers travelled along Cameroon's rivers and coast to discover the land. Ndombe learns that cutting down too many trees (deforestation) harms the environment, that municipal elections choose local council leaders, and, calmly and factually, that sexual abuse means forcing unwanted sexual contact on someone and it must always be reported to a trusted adult.
exercices.astuce: Sexual abuse must always be reported immediately to a trusted adult; it is never the child's fault.

quiz.question: How did Europeans explore Cameroon?
options: By travelling along rivers and the coast
quiz.explication: European explorers travelled along Cameroon's rivers and coast to discover the land.

quiz.question: What is deforestation?
options: Cutting down too many trees, harming the environment
quiz.explication: Deforestation is cutting down too many trees, which harms the environment.

quiz.question: What should a child do if they experience sexual abuse?
options: Tell a trusted adult right away
quiz.explication: A child should always tell a trusted adult right away; it is never the child's fault.

lecons.contenu:
The Exploration of Cameroon, Afforestation and Deforestation, Municipal Elections, and Sexual Abuse

What you will learn:

  • Learn how Europeans explored Cameroon
  • Define deforestation and its effects
  • Learn about municipal elections and how to stay safe from sexual abuse

In Douala (Week 3, Page 89), Ndombe learns how Europeans explored Cameroon, discovers deforestation, and learns about municipal elections and personal safety!

lecons.titre: More on the Exploration of Cameroon, the Coat of Arms, Obedience: Integration and Remediation
savoirs_faire: Continue explaining how Europeans explored Cameroon
Explain the importance of national emblems, focusing on the coat of arms
Practice ethical values of obedience and apply this month's lessons to daily life situations (integration, assessment and remediation)

exercices.enonce: Ndombe's teacher in Douala continues the story of European exploration of Cameroon. Ndombe then learns that the coat of arms is a national emblem showing Cameroon's unity, and practices obeying school and family rules before the month's revision.
exercices.astuce: The coat of arms is a national emblem that represents Cameroon's unity and identity.

quiz.question: What does the coat of arms represent?
quiz.explication: The coat of arms is a national emblem representing Cameroon's unity and identity.

quiz.question: Why is obedience an important value?
options: It helps maintain order and respect at home and school
quiz.explication: Obedience to rules helps maintain order and respect at home and at school.

quiz.question: What should you do during an integration and remediation week?
options: Apply what you learned to daily life
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the month's lessons to real daily life situations.

lecons.contenu:
More on the Exploration of Cameroon, the Coat of Arms, Obedience: Integration and Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Continue learning about European exploration
  • Learn about the coat of arms
  • Practice obedience and review the month's lessons

In Douala (Week 4, Page 89), Ndombe continues learning about exploration, discovers the coat of arms, and reviews everything learned this month!

lecons.titre: Responsible Computer Usage & Keyboard Special Keys
savoirs_faire: Demonstrate responsible use of computers in school and beyond (clean hands, no food/drinks near computers)
Identify and state functions of special keys on a computer keyboard (Spacebar, Enter, Backspace, Shift, Caps Lock, Arrow keys)
Practice posture rules while sitting at a computer workstation

exercices.enonce: Kotto practices typing in Douala: Spacebar inserts spaces; Enter key starts new lines; Caps Lock types capital letters.
exercices.astuce: Enter key moves the cursor to the beginning of the next line.

quiz.question: Which special keyboard key is pressed to start a new line or execute a command in Douala?
quiz.explication: Enter key starts new lines and executes commands.

quiz.question: Which key creates empty spaces between words when typing?
quiz.explication: Spacebar creates spaces between words.

quiz.question: Why are food and liquids forbidden inside computer laboratories?
options: Spills damage delicate electronic circuits and attract dust and pests
quiz.explication: Spills cause electrical short-circuits.

lecons.contenu:
Responsible Computer Usage & Keyboard Special Keys

What you will learn:

  • Demonstrate responsible use of computers in school and beyond (clean hands, no food/drinks near computers)
  • Identify and state functions of special keys on a computer keyboard (Spacebar, Enter, Backspace, Shift, Caps Lock, Arrow keys)
  • Practice posture rules while sitting at a computer workstation

In Douala (Week 1, Page 130), Kotto demonstrates responsible computer use, identifies special keyboard keys (Spacebar, Enter, Shift), and practices ergonomic posture!

lecons.titre: Computer Storage Devices (Hard Drive, USB Flash, SD Card)
savoirs_faire: Define and describe computer storage devices (Hard Drive, USB Flash Drive, SD Memory Card, CD/DVD)
Differentiate internal storage (Hard Drive) from removable portable storage (USB Flash Drive, SD Card)
Explain how to safely eject USB flash drives before removing them from computer ports

exercices.enonce: Kotto uses storage devices in Douala: USB flash drives carry files between home and school; Hard drive stores operating system.
exercices.astuce: USB Flash Drives are portable storage devices for carrying digital files.

quiz.question: Which small portable storage device plugs into a USB port to carry school projects in Douala?
quiz.explication: USB Flash Drives carry digital files portably.

quiz.question: Which storage device is built inside the system unit to store all computer files permanently?
quiz.explication: Hard Drives provide main internal storage.

quiz.question: Why should pupils click 'Safely Remove Hardware / Eject' before pulling out a USB Flash Drive?
options: To prevent data corruption of saved files on the flash drive
quiz.explication: 'Safely Remove' prevents file corruption.

lecons.contenu:
Computer Storage Devices (Hard Drive, USB Flash, SD Card)

What you will learn:

  • Define and describe computer storage devices (Hard Drive, USB Flash Drive, SD Memory Card, CD/DVD)
  • Differentiate internal storage (Hard Drive) from removable portable storage (USB Flash Drive, SD Card)
  • Explain how to safely eject USB flash drives before removing them from computer ports

In Douala (Week 2, Page 130), Kotto defines computer storage devices (Hard Drive, USB Flash Drive, SD Card), and demonstrates safe ejection procedures!

lecons.titre: Shortcut Keys & Mouse Parts and Functions
savoirs_faire: Explain the importance of keyboard shortcut keys (Ctrl+C for Copy, Ctrl+V for Paste, Ctrl+S for Save, Ctrl+Z for Undo)
Identify parts of a computer mouse (Left button, Right button, Scroll wheel, Body)
Demonstrate mouse functions (single click to select, double click to open, right click for context menu, drag and drop)

exercices.enonce: Kotto uses shortcut keys in Douala: Ctrl+C copies selected text; Ctrl+V pastes text; Ctrl+S saves document.
exercices.astuce: Ctrl+S is the universal shortcut key to save your work.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut combination is used to SAVE a document in Douala?
quiz.explication: Ctrl + S saves documents.

quiz.question: Which mouse action opens a file or program folder on the desktop screen?
quiz.explication: Double-clicking opens files and folders.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut copies highlighted text into memory?
quiz.explication: Ctrl + C copies highlighted text.

lecons.contenu:
Shortcut Keys & Mouse Parts and Functions

What you will learn:

  • Explain the importance of keyboard shortcut keys (Ctrl+C for Copy, Ctrl+V for Paste, Ctrl+S for Save, Ctrl+Z for Undo)
  • Identify parts of a computer mouse (Left button, Right button, Scroll wheel, Body)
  • Demonstrate mouse functions (single click to select, double click to open, right click for context menu, drag and drop)

In Douala (Week 3, Page 130), Kotto uses keyboard shortcut keys (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+S), identifies mouse parts, and demonstrates mouse functions!

lecons.titre: Mouse Operations (Cut/Paste Objects) & Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Use the mouse to scroll, select, cut, copy, and paste objects/files on the desktop screen
Organize files inside created folders on desktop
Apply acquired ICT KSA to solve daily life situations and complete November ICT integration

exercices.enonce: Kotto organizes files on desktop in Douala: Create folder 'Science Notes' -> Cut assignment file -> Paste into new folder.
exercices.astuce: Cut removes file from original location; Paste places it in new location.

quiz.question: Which mouse operation moves a file completely from desktop into a new folder?
quiz.explication: Cut and Paste moves files completely.

quiz.question: Which mouse part is rolled with index finger to move up and down long documents?
quiz.explication: Scroll wheel moves pages up and down.

quiz.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for Pasting copied text?
quiz.explication: Ctrl + V pastes copied content.

lecons.contenu:
Mouse Operations (Cut/Paste Objects) & Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Use the mouse to scroll, select, cut, copy, and paste objects/files on the desktop screen
  • Organize files inside created folders on desktop
  • Apply acquired ICT KSA to solve daily life situations and complete November ICT integration

In Douala (Week 4, Page 130-131), Kotto uses mouse techniques to select, cut, and paste desktop objects, organizes files in folders, and completes November ICT with excellence!

lecons.titre: Teaching Profession, Phonics 'ss/se/ce', First Conditional Tense, and Dictation
savoirs_faire: Describe the teaching profession and role of teachers in national development
Identify and pronounce words with sound patterns 'ss', 'se', 'ce' (pass, wise, nice, place, class)
Use the First Conditional Tense ('If you study hard, you will pass your exams') and write dictated paragraphs

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla describes teaching in Douala: 'If you listen to the teacher, you WILL LEARN quickly.' Sound 'ce/se': Nice, wise, place.
exercices.astuce: First conditional = If + present tense, will + base verb.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses the First Conditional Tense?
options: If you study hard, you will pass your exams
quiz.explication: If + present simple, will + verb.

quiz.question: Which word features the 'ce' soft sound pattern pronounced as /s/?
quiz.explication: 'Nice' and 'Place' have soft 'ce'.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a school Teacher in Douala?
options: Educating pupils, imparting knowledge and moral values
quiz.explication: Teachers educate and impart values.

lecons.contenu:
Teaching Profession, Phonics 'ss/se/ce', First Conditional Tense, and Dictation

What you will learn:

  • Describe the teaching profession and role of teachers in national development
  • Identify and pronounce words with sound patterns 'ss', 'se', 'ce' (pass, wise, nice, place, class)
  • Use the First Conditional Tense ('If you study hard, you will pass your exams') and write dictated paragraphs

In Douala (Week 1, Page 11), Ekwalla describes the teaching profession, pronounces 'ss/se/ce' sound words (nice, place, pass), uses the First Conditional Tense, and writes dictation!

lecons.titre: Farming Profession, Consonant Cluster 'br', Adverbs of Manner/Place, and Numbers 301-400
savoirs_faire: Carry out dialogues describing the farming profession and crops grown in Cameroon
Pronounce words with the consonant cluster 'br' (bring, broom, bread, branch, brave)
Identify and use adverbs of manner (-ly e.g. quickly, carefully), place (here, outside), and time, and write numbers 301-400

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla describes farming in Foumbot: 'The farmer works HARD in the farm. He sweeps with a BROOM.' Adverb of manner: carefully.
exercices.astuce: Adverbs of manner describe HOW an action is performed.

quiz.question: Which word is an Adverb of Manner describing how a farmer works?
quiz.explication: 'carefully' is an adverb of manner.

quiz.question: Which word contains the initial consonant cluster 'br'?
quiz.explication: 'Broom' and 'Bring' start with 'br'.

quiz.question: What is the word form of the number 350 in English?
quiz.explication: 350 is Three hundred and fifty.

lecons.contenu:
Farming Profession, Consonant Cluster 'br', Adverbs of Manner/Place, and Numbers 301-400

What you will learn:

  • Carry out dialogues describing the farming profession and crops grown in Cameroon
  • Pronounce words with the consonant cluster 'br' (bring, broom, bread, branch, brave)
  • Identify and use adverbs of manner (-ly e.g. quickly, carefully), place (here, outside), and time, and write numbers 301-400

In Foumbot & Douala (Week 2, Page 11), Ekwalla describes the farming profession, pronounces 'br' cluster words (broom, bring), uses adverbs of manner/place, and writes numbers 301-400!

lecons.titre: Medical Professions, Consonant Clusters 'gr'/'gl', Homonyms, and Numbers 801-900
savoirs_faire: Describe medical professions (doctors, nurses, pharmacists) and hospital care
Pronounce words with consonant clusters 'gr' (green, grow, grass) and 'gl' (glass, glad, globe)
Use homonyms correctly in sentences (e.g. see/sea, hear/here, write/right) and write numbers 801-900

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla describes medical care in Douala: 'The doctor cares for sick people. Homonyms: SEE the blue SEA. Number: 850 = Eight hundred and fifty.'
exercices.astuce: Homonyms are words that sound similar but have different spellings and meanings.

quiz.question: Which homonym pair completes: 'I can ___ the waves of the ___'?
quiz.explication: 'see' (vision) and 'sea' (ocean).

quiz.question: Which word starts with the consonant cluster 'gl'?
quiz.explication: 'Glass' and 'Glad' start with 'gl'.

quiz.question: What is the role of a Pharmacist in healthcare?
options: Preparing and dispensing prescribed medicines safely
quiz.explication: Pharmacists dispense medicines.

lecons.contenu:
Medical Professions, Consonant Clusters 'gr'/'gl', Homonyms, and Numbers 801-900

What you will learn:

  • Describe medical professions (doctors, nurses, pharmacists) and hospital care
  • Pronounce words with consonant clusters 'gr' (green, grow, grass) and 'gl' (glass, glad, globe)
  • Use homonyms correctly in sentences (e.g. see/sea, hear/here, write/right) and write numbers 801-900

In Douala (Week 3, Page 11-12), Ekwalla describes medical professions (doctors, nurses), pronounces 'gr'/'gl' cluster words (green, glass), uses homonyms (see/sea), and writes numbers 801-900!

lecons.titre: Carpentry & Building Trades, Prose Passages, Comparative Adjectives, and Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Describe carpentry and building construction trades (carpenter, saw, wood, building furniture)
Read prose passages silently and answer comprehension questions
Construct sentences using comparative adjectives and complete December English integration

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla describes carpentry in Douala: 'The carpenter uses a sharp saw to cut timber. Comparative: Mahogany wood is STRONGER than pine wood.'
exercices.astuce: Carpenters construct wooden structures, doors, and school desks.

quiz.question: Which tool does a Carpenter use for cutting wooden timber into planks?
quiz.explication: Carpenters use saws to cut timber.

quiz.question: Which comparative adjective completes: 'Hardwood is ___ than soft plywood'?
quiz.explication: 'stronger' compares two items.

quiz.question: What product is crafted by skilled carpenters for school classrooms?
quiz.explication: Carpenters build wooden desks and chairs.

lecons.contenu:
Carpentry & Building Trades, Prose Passages, Comparative Adjectives, and Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Describe carpentry and building construction trades (carpenter, saw, wood, building furniture)
  • Read prose passages silently and answer comprehension questions
  • Construct sentences using comparative adjectives and complete December English integration

In Douala (Week 4, Page 12), Ekwalla describes carpentry and building trades, reads prose passages, uses comparative adjectives, and completes December English with excellence!

lecons.titre: Multiples of Numbers to 5000, Finite Sets, Weight Operations, Perimeters, and Map Axes
savoirs_faire: Find multiples of numbers up to 5,000 (e.g. multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20...) and describe finite sets
Perform multiplication and division of weight (e.g. 4 kg 200 g × 3 = 12 kg 600 g; 8 kg 400 g ÷ 2 = 4 kg 200 g)
Calculate the perimeter of squares (P = 4 × s) and rectangles (P = 2 × (l + w)) and read coordinates on x,y maps

exercices.enonce: Ndombe calculates perimeter in Douala: Square side = 6 cm -> P = 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Weight: 4 kg 200 g × 3 = 12 kg 600 g.
exercices.astuce: Perimeter of a square = 4 × side length.

quiz.question: What is the Perimeter of a square with a side length of 6 cm?
What is 4 kg 200 g × 3 in weight multiplication?
Which set contains multiples of 5 less than 25?
quiz.explication: 5, 10, 15, 20 are multiples of 5.

lecons.contenu:
Multiples of Numbers to 5000, Finite Sets, Weight Operations, Perimeters, and Map Axes

What you will learn:

  • Find multiples of numbers up to 5,000 (e.g. multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20...) and describe finite sets
  • Perform multiplication and division of weight (e.g. 4 kg 200 g × 3 = 12 kg 600 g; 8 kg 400 g ÷ 2 = 4 kg 200 g)
  • Calculate the perimeter of squares (P = 4 × s) and rectangles (P = 2 × (l + w)) and read coordinates on x,y maps

In Douala (Week 1, Page 23), Ndombe finds multiples of numbers up to 5,000, multiplies/divides weight, calculates perimeters of squares/rectangles, and reads map coordinates!

lecons.titre: Common Multiples, Infinite Sets, and Capacity Measurements (Liters & Milliliters)
savoirs_faire: Find common multiples of given pairs of numbers (e.g. common multiples of 3 and 4: 12, 24, 36...)
Describe Infinite sets (sets with endless un-countable elements e.g. set of even numbers {2,4,6,8...})
Use metric measurements of capacity (liters, milliliters: 1 L = 1000 mL) to solve addition and subtraction capacity problems

exercices.enonce: Ndombe converts capacity in Douala: 3 Liters = 3000 mL. Common multiples of 3 and 4 = 12, 24, 36. Infinite set: {2, 4, 6, 8...}.
exercices.astuce: 1 Liter (L) = 1000 milliliters (mL).

quiz.question: How many milliliters (mL) are equal to 3 Liters (L)?
What is the smallest Common Multiple of 3 and 4?
quiz.explication: 12 is the smallest common multiple.

quiz.question: Which of the following is an example of an Infinite Set?
options: Set of days of the week
quiz.explication: Counting numbers go on endlessly without bound.

lecons.contenu:
Common Multiples, Infinite Sets, and Capacity Measurements (Liters & Milliliters)

What you will learn:

  • Find common multiples of given pairs of numbers (e.g. common multiples of 3 and 4: 12, 24, 36...)
  • Describe Infinite sets (sets with endless un-countable elements e.g. set of even numbers {2,4,6,8...})
  • Use metric measurements of capacity (liters, milliliters: 1 L = 1000 mL) to solve addition and subtraction capacity problems

In Douala (Week 2, Page 23), Ndombe finds common multiples, describes infinite sets ({1,2,3...}), converts capacity (3 L = 3000 mL), and solves capacity addition/subtraction!

lecons.titre: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM), Finite vs Infinite Sets, Converting Capacity Units, and Area of a Triangle
savoirs_faire: Explain the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of numbers and solve problems involving LCM (e.g. LCM of 4 and 6 is 12)
Distinguish between finite sets (countable elements) and infinite sets (endless elements), and convert from one capacity unit to another (e.g. litres to millilitres)
Calculate the area of triangles, and identify and draw parallel and intersecting lines, indicating the points of intersection

exercices.enonce: Manyi in Bafut lists multiples of 4 and 6 to find their LCM (12), then converts 2 litres of palm oil into millilitres (2000 mL).
exercices.astuce: The LCM is the smallest number that appears in both lists of multiples.

quiz.question: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
quiz.explication: 12 is the smallest common multiple of 4 and 6.

quiz.question: Which set is infinite?
options: The set of all even numbers
The set of days in a week
quiz.explication: Even numbers go on forever, so the set is infinite.

quiz.question: The area of a triangle is calculated using which measurement?
quiz.explication: Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height.

lecons.contenu:
Lowest Common Multiple (LCM), Finite vs Infinite Sets, Converting Capacity Units, and Area of a Triangle

What you will learn:

  • Find the LCM of numbers
  • Distinguish finite/infinite sets and convert capacity units
  • Calculate the area of a triangle and identify parallel/intersecting lines

In Bafut (Week 3, Page 24), Manyi finds the LCM of numbers, converts litres to millilitres, and calculates the area of a triangle!

lecons.titre: Types of Fractions, Addition of Capacity (with/without Carrying), Area of a Rectangle, and Integration
savoirs_faire: Identify the different types of fractions (proper, improper, mixed)
Add capacities with and without carrying (e.g. 3 L 600 mL + 2 L 800 mL = 6 L 400 mL)
Calculate the area of a rectangle (Area = length × width) and use K.S.A to solve daily mathematical problems (integration, assessment and remediation)

exercices.enonce: Manyi in Bafut identifies the fraction 3/4 (proper) and 5/4 (improper), then adds 3 L 600 mL of water and 2 L 800 mL, carrying over to get 6 L 400 mL.
exercices.astuce: When adding capacity, if millilitres reach 1000 or more, carry 1 litre over, just like carrying in normal addition.

quiz.question: Which is a proper fraction?
quiz.explication: In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator.

quiz.question: How do you calculate the area of a rectangle?
quiz.explication: Area of a rectangle = length × width.

lecons.contenu:
Types of Fractions, Addition of Capacity (with/without Carrying), Area of a Rectangle, and Integration

What you will learn:

  • Identify types of fractions
  • Add capacities with and without carrying
  • Calculate the area of a rectangle

In Bafut (Week 4, Page 24), Manyi identifies fractions, adds capacities with carrying, and calculates the area of a rectangle to close the month on Occupations!

lecons.titre: Care of the Female Reproductive System, Weaving a Raffia Bag, and the Importance and Conservation of Plants
savoirs_faire: Say how to care for the female reproductive system (personal cleanliness, hygiene)
Continue weaving a raffia bag using local materials
Explain the importance of plants and why they must be conserved

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that daily washing and good hygiene keep the female reproductive system healthy, then Ekwalla continues weaving a raffia bag and learns why the trees near the school must be protected.
exercices.astuce: Daily washing and good personal hygiene are the main ways to care for the reproductive organs, just like any other body part.

quiz.question: How should the female reproductive system be cared for?
options: Through daily washing and good hygiene
quiz.explication: Good personal hygiene, including daily washing, cares for the female reproductive system.

quiz.question: What is Ekwalla weaving this week?
quiz.explication: Ekwalla continues weaving a raffia bag from local materials.

quiz.question: Why must plants be conserved?
options: Because they are important to people and the environment
quiz.explication: Plants give us food, air, and materials, so they must be protected and conserved.

lecons.contenu:
Care of the Female Reproductive System, Weaving a Raffia Bag, and the Importance and Conservation of Plants

What you will learn:

  • Learn how to care for the female reproductive system through hygiene
  • Continue weaving a raffia bag
  • Discover the importance of plants and why they must be conserved

In Douala (Week 1, Page 32), Ekwalla learns about body hygiene, weaves a raffia bag, and discovers why plants must be protected!

lecons.titre: The Meaning of HIV/AIDS, Types and Materials Used in Plumbing, and Common Diseases
savoirs_faire: Explain the meaning of HIV/AIDS (a serious illness caused by a virus that weakens the body's defences)
Name the different types of plumbing and the materials plumbers use (pipes, taps, fittings)
Name common diseases found in the community

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that HIV/AIDS is a serious illness caused by a virus, then Ekwalla visits a plumber who shows different pipes and taps, and learns the names of common diseases like malaria and cough.
exercices.astuce: HIV/AIDS is caused by a virus that attacks the body's ability to fight illness; it is a health topic to understand calmly and factually.

quiz.question: What is HIV/AIDS?
options: A serious illness caused by a virus that weakens the body's defences
quiz.explication: HIV/AIDS is caused by a virus that weakens the body's ability to fight illness.

quiz.question: Which of these is a material used by a plumber?
quiz.explication: Plumbers work with pipes, taps, and fittings to carry water.

quiz.question: Which of these is a common disease in the community?
quiz.explication: Malaria is a common disease found in many communities.

lecons.contenu:
The Meaning of HIV/AIDS, Types and Materials Used in Plumbing, and Common Diseases

What you will learn:

  • Learn the meaning of HIV/AIDS
  • Discover the types and materials used in plumbing
  • Name common diseases in the community

In Douala (Week 2, Page 32), Ekwalla learns what HIV/AIDS means, visits a plumber to see pipes and taps, and names common diseases in the community!

lecons.titre: Mode of Transmission of HIV/AIDS, Plumbing Materials and Other Uses, and Air and Water Borne Diseases
savoirs_faire: Explain how HIV/AIDS is transmitted (through infected blood, unprotected sex, from mother to child)
Name plumbing materials and their other uses in the home
Identify air-borne and water-borne diseases and how to prevent them

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains, factually and calmly, that HIV/AIDS can pass from an infected person to another through infected blood, unprotected sex, or from a mother to her child. Ekwalla also learns that pipes can carry water for drinking and washing, and that diseases like cough and cholera spread through dirty air and water.
exercices.astuce: HIV/AIDS spreads mainly through infected blood, unprotected sex, and from mother to child — knowing this helps prevention.

quiz.question: How can HIV/AIDS be transmitted?
options: Through infected blood, unprotected sex, or from mother to child
quiz.explication: HIV/AIDS spreads through infected blood, unprotected sex, and from mother to child, not through everyday contact.

quiz.question: What can plumbing pipes be used for at home?
options: Carrying water for drinking and washing
quiz.explication: Plumbing pipes carry water to taps for drinking, washing, and other household uses.

quiz.question: Which of these is a water-borne disease?
quiz.explication: Cholera spreads through contaminated (dirty) water.

lecons.contenu:
Mode of Transmission of HIV/AIDS, Plumbing Materials and Other Uses, and Air and Water Borne Diseases

What you will learn:

  • Learn how HIV/AIDS is transmitted
  • Discover other uses of plumbing materials
  • Identify air-borne and water-borne diseases

In Douala (Week 3, Page 33), Ekwalla learns how HIV/AIDS spreads, discovers other uses of plumbing materials, and identifies air and water borne diseases!

lecons.titre: How HIV/AIDS Can Be Prevented, the Steps of Plumbing Work: Integration and Remediation
savoirs_faire: Say how HIV/AIDS can be prevented (avoiding infected blood, protected sex, faithfulness, testing)
Describe the steps followed in simple plumbing work
Apply knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired this month to daily life situations (integration, assessment and remediation)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains, calmly and factually, that HIV/AIDS can be prevented by avoiding contact with infected blood, protected behaviour, faithfulness, and regular health testing. Ekwalla then reviews the steps a plumber follows: checking the pipe, cutting it to size, joining it, and testing for leaks.
exercices.astuce: Prevention of HIV/AIDS relies on avoiding infected blood, protected behaviour, faithfulness, and testing — simple, factual health knowledge.

quiz.question: How can HIV/AIDS be prevented?
options: Avoiding infected blood, protected behaviour, and testing
quiz.explication: Prevention relies on avoiding infected blood, protected behaviour, faithfulness, and regular testing.

quiz.question: What is the first step in simple plumbing work?
quiz.explication: A plumber first checks the pipe before cutting, joining, and testing it.

quiz.question: What should you do during an integration and remediation week?
options: Apply what you learned to daily life
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the month's lessons to real daily life situations.

lecons.contenu:
How HIV/AIDS Can Be Prevented, the Steps of Plumbing Work: Integration and Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Learn how HIV/AIDS can be prevented
  • Review the steps of simple plumbing work
  • Review the month's lessons about Occupations

In Douala (Week 4, Page 33), Ekwalla learns how HIV/AIDS can be prevented, reviews the steps of plumbing work, and reviews everything learned this month about Occupations!

lecons.titre: Les métiers et professions, lexique des Professions, et le féminin des noms de métiers
savoirs_faire: Présenter et décrire les métiers de ses parents et de son entourage ('Mon père est mécanicien, ma mère est enseignante')
Enrichir son vocabulaire des professions (agriculteur, docteur, couturier, menuisier, commerçant)
Former le féminin des noms de métiers (un enseignant -> une enseignante, un couturier -> une couturière)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla et Ngo Mbog à Douala (Cameroun) : 'Son père est UN COUTURIER, sa mère est UNE COUTURIÈRE. Un enseignant -> Une enseignante.'
exercices.astuce: Le féminin des noms de métiers se forme souvent en ajoutant -e (enseignant -> enseignante) ou -ère (couturier -> couturière).

quiz.question: Quel est le féminin du nom de métier 'couturier' ?
quiz.explication: 'couturier' devient 'couturière' au féminin.

quiz.question: Quel est le féminin du nom 'enseignant' ?
quiz.explication: 'enseignant' devient 'enseignante'.

quiz.question: Quel nom désigne la personne qui fabrique et répare les vêtements ?
quiz.explication: Le couturier fabrique des vêtements.

lecons.contenu:
Les métiers et professions, lexique des Professions, et le féminin des noms de métiers

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Présenter et décrire les métiers de ses parents et de son entourage ('Mon père est mécanicien, ma mère est enseignante')
  • Enrichir son vocabulaire des professions (agriculteur, docteur, couturier, menuisier, commerçant)
  • Former le féminin des noms de métiers (un enseignant -> une enseignante, un couturier -> une couturière)

À Douala au Cameroun (Semaine 1, Page 43), Ekwalla et Ngo Mbog présentent les métiers de leur entourage, étudient le lexique des professions, et forment le féminin des noms de métiers !

lecons.titre: Les outils des métiers et lieux de travail, les prépositions de lieu, et le son [IN]
savoirs_faire: Associer chaque métier à son outil et à son lieu de travail ('Le médecin travaille à l'hôpital avec un stéthoscope')
Employer les prépositions de lieu (à, chez, dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière)
Orthographier le son [IN/AIN/EIN] (matin, pain, frein, chemin, magasin)

exercices.enonce: Ndombe et Ngo Mbog à Buea (Cameroun) : 'Le mécanicien travaille DANS son garage. Il achète du pain (son [IN]) le MATIN chez le boulanger.'
exercices.astuce: Prépositions de lieu : DANS (intérieur), CHEZ (personne), SUR (dessus).

quiz.question: Quelle préposition de lieu convient dans : 'Ndombe va ___ le médecin à Buea' ?
quiz.explication: 'chez' s'utilise devant une personne.

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots contient l'orthographe du son [IN] dans 'pain' ?
quiz.explication: 'Pain' et 'Matin' contiennent le son [IN].

quiz.question: Où travaille le médecin pour soigner les malades ?
options: À l'hôpital / au centre de santé
quiz.explication: Le médecin travaille à l'hôpital.

lecons.contenu:
Les outils des métiers et lieux de travail, les prépositions de lieu, et le son [IN]

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Associer chaque métier à son outil et à son lieu de travail ('Le médecin travaille à l'hôpital avec un stéthoscope')
  • Employer les prépositions de lieu (à, chez, dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière)
  • Orthographier le son [IN/AIN/EIN] (matin, pain, frein, chemin, magasin)

À Buea au Cameroun (Semaine 2, Page 44), Ndombe et Ngo Mbog associent les métiers à leurs lieux de travail, emploient les prépositions de lieu (chez, dans), et orthographient le son [IN] !

lecons.titre: Description d'un métier de son choix, verbes pronominaux au présent, et évaluation de décembre
savoirs_faire: Rédiger un court texte descriptif sur le métier que l'on aimerait exercer plus tard
Conjuguer les verbes pronominaux au présent (se lever -> je me lève, s'habiller -> il s'habille)
Réaliser avec succès l'évaluation du mois de décembre

exercices.enonce: Bikoy et Ngo Mbog à Bamenda (Cameroun) : 'Le boulanger SE LÈVE tôt le matin (verbe pronominal). Plus tard, je veux être ingénieur.'
exercices.astuce: Verbes pronominaux : je me..., tu te..., il se..., nous nous..., vous vous..., ils se...

quiz.question: Quelle est la forme du verbe pronominal 'se lever' avec 'il' au présent ?
quiz.explication: 'il se lève' est la forme pronominale correcte.

quiz.question: Quelle est la forme de 'se laver' avec 'nous' au présent ?
quiz.explication: 'nous nous lavons' répète le pronom réflexif.

quiz.question: Quel métier consiste à réparer les moteurs des voitures et taxis ?
quiz.explication: Le mécanicien répare les véhicules.

lecons.contenu:
Description d'un métier de son choix, verbes pronominaux au présent, et évaluation de décembre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Rédiger un court texte descriptif sur le métier que l'on aimerait exercer plus tard
  • Conjuguer les verbes pronominaux au présent (se lever -> je me lève, s'habiller -> il s'habille)
  • Réaliser avec succès l'évaluation du mois de décembre

À Bamenda au Cameroun (Semaine 3, Page 44-45), Bikoy et Ngo Mbog décrivent le métier de leur choix, conjuguent les verbes pronominaux au présent (se lève, nous lavons), et réussissent l'évaluation de décembre !

lecons.titre: Religious Movements in Cameroon, Soil and Its Types, Legislative Elections, and Drug Abuse

Religious Movements in Cameroon, Soil and Its Types, Legislative Elections, and Drug Abuse

lecons.titre: Animism in Cameroon, Soil Types and Characteristics, the Home, and Honesty
savoirs_faire: Explain the origin and practice of animism in Cameroon
List soil types and their characteristics
State the rules and regulations of a home, and practice the ethical value of honesty

quiz.question: What does honesty mean?
options: Taking things that are not yours

lecons.contenu:
Animism in Cameroon, Soil Types and Characteristics, the Home, and Honesty

  • Learn about animism in Cameroon

In Bamenda (Week 2, Page 90), Bikoy learns about animism, discovers soil characteristics, and practices honesty at home!

Islam and Christianity: Origins, Soil Erosion and Its Causes, Presidential Elections, and Peace

Islam and Christianity Continued, More on Soil Erosion and Its Causes: Integration and Remediation

Headers, Footers, Bullets & Page Numbering

lecons.titre: Types of Fractions, Improper to Mixed Conversion, Disjointed Sets, Capacity Subtraction, and x,y Plotting
savoirs_faire: Identify types of fractions (Proper fraction 3/4, Improper fraction 7/4, Mixed number 1 3/4)

quiz.question: What is the mixed number 2 1/3 converted into an Improper Fraction?

lecons.contenu:
Mixed to Improper Conversion, Empty Sets, Capacity Operations, Area of Circle (A = πr²), and x,y Shapes

lecons.titre: The Effects of Drugs, More Causes of Accidents, and the Definition and Types of STDs
